Kim / team,

High-level recommendation (working draft):
1) Preferred path: Splunk HEC over HTTPS with short-lived HEC tokens + optional client mTLS.
   - Why: HEC preserves structured JSON fields, supports batching, and is firewall-friendly (HTTPS 443).
2) Fallback: TCP syslog over TLS (RFC5425) to a collector inside Acme.
   - If they insist on UDP syslog we recommend encapsulating in an internal forwarder to add TLS.
3) Deployment pattern: sidecar forwarder colocated with Redwood private runtime (process or container) that performs:
   - Local buffering, batching, and backpressure control.
   - Upstream auth: HEC token for initial auth; mTLS established if customer requests cert-based trust.
   - Egress proxy handling: forwarder must support HTTP CONNECT tunneling or proxy negotiation; if SNI inspection is enforced they need to allow SNI for the HEC host.

Quick config snippet (Splunk HEC over HTTPS):
- endpoint: https://splunk.acmecloud.com:8088/services/collector
- headers: Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>
- tls:verify: true
- tls:client_cert: optional (path to crt)

I'll draft a short doc (redwood-private-forwarder-pattern.md) with diagrams and sample conf. Attaching draft.

Diego
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-forwarder-pattern.md

Couple of operational notes to include in the runbook:
- Firewall rules: allow outbound TCP 443 to the splunk HEC hostname (we should provide FQDN and ASN ranges if available). Avoid asking customers to open wide IP ranges.
- Egress proxy: if Acme's proxy does TLS inspection, we need either:
  a) a customer exception to preserve end-to-end TLS to HEC (preferred), or
  b) exchange intermediate cert for signing, and run acceptance tests with their proxy team.
- DNS: ensure private runtime can resolve the HEC host via customer DNS or provide an IP whitelisting fallback.
- NAT and connection scaling: forwarder must multiplex connections to upstream to avoid per-instance ephemeral port exhaustion; include connection pooling in the sample config.

I'll add a checklist for network-ops handoff and a short test plan (connectivity, token rotation, rotation failure behavior).

Jonas
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment: SIEM ingest, proxy auth, and firewall expectations

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. We're aligned on the Splunk HEC-over-HTTPS pattern as our primary recommendation with a TCP syslog/TLS fallback. Attached are the artifacts we promised: sample-splunk-hec-config.conf and private-ingest-checklist.yaml.

Summary for your network/security team:
- Transport: Splunk HEC (HTTPS / TCP 443).
- Auth: HEC token by default. mTLS supported if you prefer cert-based client auth; we can provide CSR instructions.
- Egress proxy: our forwarder supports HTTP CONNECT and proxy negotiation. If your proxy performs TLS inspection, please either allow an exception for the HEC host to preserve E2E TLS or provide your proxy's CA to install for test verification.
- Firewall: allow outbound TCP 443 to splunk.acmecloud.com (we'll supply FQDN + ASN/IP ranges in the runbook).
- Test plan: we will run a connectivity check, token-based ingest test, and a failure-recovery test (retention during transient network failures).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you want mTLS enabled or token-only.
2) Confirm availability for a 30 min call on 2027-04-29 (Marissa will send invite).
3) Share any proxy/inspection policies that would impact SNI or hostname preservation.

Thanks — attaching artifacts and the draft runbook.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Deployments (Private)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-splunk-hec-config.conf, private-ingest-checklist.yaml
